barkerde@nmenergy.com writes to the NYISO_TECH_EXCHANGE Discussion List: After going through the Representative, Hot Line, and finally turning to the TIE (yes, last resort), I have had all my questions and concerns addressed. MPs using the forum helped tremendously. However, the written and phone discussions with a NYISO staff person who took a lot of time and patience helped me understand that, while not the ideal solution, the combination of bid guarantees, bid babysitting, ECAs, and a healthy dose of caution, the resulting procedures are the best that can be crafted at this time.

I have had about five alignments done here over the past few years and the work was always good. Joel is always very nice. However, Ken, the older man, is usually in a bad mood and probably needs to retire. The last time I was there, he was very short and rude.

I ate dinner here family-style with two friends, and all the food tasted good. The decor is outdated and looks like a cliché 1980s Chinese restaurant, but the excellent service compensates for this. The staff is friendly, patient, and kind. They recognized my friends, who are repeat customers, which was a nice touch. My only disappointment is that they do not serve Cantonese-style chow mein or chow fun.

There were issues with the payment, and she wasn't just inflexible—she was downright snooty about it. She actually suggested removing the anesthesia to lower the cost. Um, I'm having oral surgery here, lady. A doctor is going to be drilling into my face and blood will be spattering everywhere. I think I'll keep the anesthesia. Do I look like the guy from A Million Little Pieces?

Dr. Day prepares thoroughly for his patients. He genuinely cares about their comfort during procedures. I never experienced any pain or discomfort during any of the procedures at Dr. Day's office. Each time I had a procedure done—whether it was an implant removal, implant placement, or gum adjustment—the healing went smoothly. I never left his office and later developed an infection or any other post-surgical complications. I am a musician, and I look forward to returning to playing my flute, piccolo, and oboe.

I had my car detailed today, and not only did they do an excellent job, but when I opened the cup holder, I found a graduation gift (a Tiffany necklace) that I thought had been lost long ago. Their quality work and honesty have definitely earned my future business.

My steak was close to $30 alone. For a place that bills itself as a wine bar, I was disappointed with the by-the-glass choices. I guess if you are only searching for a good-tasting steak and you don't know how to cook, Fleming's is the place to go. "Depillo, Raymond V." <Raymond.Depillo@pseg.com> writes to the NYISO_TECH_EXCHANGE Discussion List: Certainly, the problem Don identified is legitimate and can still occur. However, with the implementation of the ECAs, we have seen a change in bidding behavior at the interfaces - HAMs no longer bid at or near the caps. Thus, by changing HAM prices of accepted DAM transactions to something like +/- $500, you can be reasonably sure your transaction will flow.

I had three separate complaints, and she handled each one very professionally. While I was shopping, she approached me and gave me a $3 coupon for my inconvenience. A note to corporate: this is the level of customer service you should aim for in every store.
